layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Many real-world vision problems suffer from inherent ambiguities. In clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applications for example, it might not be clear from a CT scan alone which par-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ticular region is cancer tissue. Therefore a group of graders typically produces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a set of diverse but plausible segmentations. We consider the task of learning a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution over segmentations given an input. To this end we propose a generative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation model based on a combination of a U-Net with a conditional vari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ational autoencoder that is capable of efficiently producing an unlimited number

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of plausible hypotheses. We show on a lung abnormalities segmentation task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and on a Cityscapes segmentation task that our model reproduces the possible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation variants as well as the frequencies with which they occur, doing so

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significantly better than published approaches. These models could have a high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: impact in real-world applications, such as being used as clinical decision-making

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: algorithms accounting for multiple plausible semantic segmentation hypotheses to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provide possible diagnoses and recommend further actions to resolve the present

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ambiguities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The semantic segmentation task assigns a class label to each pixel in an image. While in many

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases the context in the image provides sufficient information to resolve the ambiguities in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mapping, there exists an important class of images where even the full image context is not sufficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to resolve all ambiguities. Such ambiguities are common in medical imaging applications, e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in lung abnormalities segmentation from CT images. A lesion might be clearly visible, but the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information about whether it is cancer tissue or not might not be available from this image alone.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Similar ambiguities are also present in photos. E.g. a part of fur visible under the sofa might belong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a cat or a dog, but it is not possible from the image alone to resolve this ambiguity². Most existing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation algorithms either provide only one likely consistent hypothesis (e.g., “all pixels belong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a cat") or a pixel-wise probability (e.g., “each pixel is 50% cat and 50% dog").

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Especially in medical applications where a subsequent diagnosis or a treatment depends on the seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation map, an algorithm that only provides the most likely hypothesis might lead to misdiagnoses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: ambiguous class definition (e.g. the concepts of desk vs. table). For the presented work this differentiation is not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and sub-optimal treatment. Providing only pixel-wise probabilities ignores all co-variances between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pixels, which makes a subsequent analysis much more difficult if not impossible. If multiple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistent hypotheses are provided, these can be directly propagated into the next step in a diagnosis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pipeline, they can be used to suggest further diagnostic tests to resolve the ambiguities, or an expert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with access to additional information can select the appropriate one(s) for the subsequent steps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Here we present a segmentation framework that provides multiple segmentation hypotheses for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ambiguous images (Fig. 1a). Our framework combines a conditional variational auto encoder (CVAE)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [2, 3, 4, 5] which can model complex distributions, with a U-Net [6] which delivers state-of-the-art

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentations in many medical application domains. A low-dimensional latent space encodes the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: possible segmentation variants. A random sample from this space is injected into the U-Net to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: produce the corresponding segmentation map. One key feature of this architecture is the ability to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model the joint probability of all pixels in the segmentation map. This results in multiple segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maps, where each of them provides a consistent interpretation of the whole image. Furthermore our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: framework is able to also learn hypotheses that have a low probability and to predict them with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding frequency. We demonstrate these features on a lung abnormalities segmentation task,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where each lesion has been segmented independently by four experts, and on the Cityscapes dataset,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where we artificially flip labels with a certain frequency during training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A body of work with different approaches towards probabilistic and multi-modal segmentation exists.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The most common approaches provide independent pixel-wise probabilities [7, 8]. These models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: induce a probability distribution by using dropout over spatial features. Whereas this strategy fulfills

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this line of work's objective of quantifying the pixel-wise uncertainty, it produces inconsistent outputs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A simple way to produce plausible hypotheses is to learn an ensemble of (deep) models [9]. While

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the outputs produced by ensembles are consistent, they are not necessarily diverse and ensembles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are typically not able to learn the rare variants as their members are trained independently. In order

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to overcome this, several approaches train models jointly using the oracle set loss [10], i.e. a loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that only accounts for the closest prediction to the ground truth. This has been explored in [11] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [1] using an ensemble of deep networks, and in [12] and [13] using one common deep network with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: M heads. While multi-head approaches may have the capacity to capture a diverse set of variants,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they are not equipped to learn the occurrence frequencies of individual variants. Two common

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disadvantages of both ensembles and M heads models are their ungraceful scaling to large numbers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of hypotheses, and their requirement of fixing the number of allowed hypotheses at training time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Another set of approaches to produce multiple diverse solutions relies on graphical models, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: junction chains [14], and more generally Markov Random Fields [15, 16, 17, 18]. While many of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The task of image-to-image translation [19] tackles a very similar problem: an under-constrained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain transfer of images needs to be learned. Many of the recent approaches employ generative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adversarial networks (GANs) which are known to suffer from challenges such as mode-collapse' [20].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In an attempt to solve the mode-collapse problem, the bicycleGAN' [21] involves a component that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is similar in architecture to ours. In contrast to our proposed architecture, their model encompasses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a fixed prior distribution and during training their posterior distribution is only conditioned on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: output image. Very recent work on generating appearances given a shape encoding [22] also combines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a U-Net with a VAE, and was developed concurrently to ours. In contrast to our proposal, their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training requires an additional pretrained VGG-net that is employed as a reconstruction loss. Finally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in [23] is proposed a probabilistic model for structured outputs based on optimizing the dissimilarity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coefficient [24] between the ground truth and predicted distributions. The resultant approach is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assessed on the task of hand pose estimation, that is, predicting the location of 14 joints, arguably a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: simpler space compared to the space of segmentations we consider here. Similarly to the approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presented below, they inject latent variables at a later stage of the network architecture.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The main contributions of this work are: (1) Our framework provides consistent segmentation maps

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instead of pixel-wise probabilities and can therefore give a joint likelihood of modes. (2) Our model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can induce arbitrarily complex output distributions including the occurrence of very rare modes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and is able to learn calibrated probabilities of segmentation modes. (3) Sampling from our model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is computationally cheap. (4) In contrast to many existing applications of deep generative models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that can only be qualitatively evaluated, our application and datasets allow quantitative performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation including penalization of missing modes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Network Architecture and Training Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Performance Measures and Baseline Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this section we first present the metric used to assess the performance of all approaches, and then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: describe each competitor approach used in the comparisons.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Performance measures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As it is common in the semantic segmentation literature, we employ the intersection over union

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (IoU) as a measure to compare a pair of segmentations. However, in the present case, we not only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: want to compare a deterministic prediction with a unique ground truth, but rather we are interested

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in comparing distributions of segmentations. To do

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we use the generalized energy distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [26, 27, 28], which leverages distances between observations:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Baseline methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: With the aim of providing context for the performance of our proposed approach we compare against

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a range of baselines. To the best of our knowledge there exists no other work that has considered

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capturing a distribution over multi-modal segmentations and has measured the agreement with such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a distribution. For fair comparison, we train the baseline models whose architectures are depicted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Fig. 2 in the exact same manner as we train ours. The baseline methods all involve the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net architecture, i.e. they share the same core component and thus employ comparable numbers of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learnable parameters in the segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space in image-to-image translation tasks, they employ an adversarial discriminator as additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: net that is not conditioned on the input either.

layout_dets.text: In all cases we examine the models' performance when drawing a different number of samples (1, 4,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A quantitative evaluation of multiple segmentation predictions per image requires annotations from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple labelers. Here we consider two datasets: The LIDC-IDRI dataset [32, 33, 34] which contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 annotations per input, and the Cityscapes dataset [35], which we artificially modify by adding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: synonymous classes to introduce uncertainty in the way concepts are labelled.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Lung abnormalities segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The LIDC-IDRI dataset [32, 33, 34] contains 1018 lung CT scans from 1010 lung patients with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manual lesion segmentations from four experts. This dataset is a good representation of the typical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ambiguities that appear in CT scans. For each scan, 4 radiologists (from a total of 12) provided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotation masks for lesions that they independently detected and considered to be abnormal. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use the masks resulting from a second reading in which the radiologists were shown the anonymized

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations of the others and were allowed to make adjustments to their own masks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For our experiments we split this dataset into a training set composed of 722 patients, a validation set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composed of 144 patients, and a test set composed of the remaining 144 patients. We then resampled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3 Analysis of the Latent Space

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The embedding of the segmentation variants in a low-dimensional latent space allows a qualitative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis of the internal representation of our model. For a 2D or 3D latent space we can directly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: visualize where the segmentation variants get assigned. See Appendix A for details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Discussion and conclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our first set of experiments demonstrates that our proposed architecture provides consistent segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation maps that closely match the multi-modal ground-truth distributions given by the expert graders

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the lung abnormalities task and by the combinatorial ground-truth segmentation modes in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cityscapes task. The employed IoU-based energy distance measures whether the models' individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: samples are both coherent as well as whether they are produced with the expected frequencies. It

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not only penalizes predicted segmentation variants that are far away from the ground truth, but also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: penalizes missing variants. On this task the Probabilistic U-Net is able to significantly outperform the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered baselines, indicating its capability to model the joint likelihood of segmentation variants.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The second type of experiments demonstrates that our model scales to complex output distributions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: including the occurrence of very rare modes. With 32 discrete modes of largely differing occurrence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: likelihoods (0.5% to 10.9%), the Cityscapes task requires the ability to closely match complex data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distributions. Here too our model performs best and picks the segmentation modes very close to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: expected frequencies, all the way into the regime of very unlikely modes, thus defying mode-collapse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and exhibiting excellent probability calibration. As an additional advantage our model scales to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such large numbers of modes without requiring any prior assumptions on the number of modes or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hypotheses.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The lower performance of the baseline models relative to our proposition can be attributed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: design choices of these models. While the Dropout U-Net successfully models the pixel-wise data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution (Fig. 8a bottom right, in the Appendix), such pixel-wise mixtures of variants can not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: valid hypotheses in themselves (see Fig. 3). The U-Net Ensemble's members are trained independently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and each of them can only learn the most likely segmentation variant as attested to by Fig. 8b. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast to that the closely related M-Heads model can pick up on multiple discrete segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modes, due to the joint training procedure that enables diversity. The training does however not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allow to correctly represent frequencies and requires knowledge of the number of present variants

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (see Fig. 9a, in the Appendix). Furthermore neither the U-Net Ensemble, nor the M-Heads can deal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the combinatorial explosion of segmentation variants when multiple aspects vary independently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of each other. The Image2Image VAE shares similarities with our model, but as its prior is fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and not conditioned on the input image, it can not learn to capture variant frequencies by allocating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding probability mass to the respective latent space regions. Fig. 17 in the Appendix shows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a severe miss-calibration of variant likelihoods on the lung abnormalities task that is also reflected in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its corresponding energy distance. Furthermore, in this architecture, the latent samples are fed into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the U-Net's encoder path, while we feed in the samples just after the decoder path. This design choice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the Image2Image VAE requires the model to carry the latent information all the way through the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: U-Net core, while simultaneously performing the recognition required for segmentation, which might

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additionally complicate training (see analysis in Appendix D). Beside that, our design choice of late

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: injection has the additional advantage that we can produce a large set of samples for a given image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at a very low computational cost: for each new sample from the latent space only the network part

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after the injection needs to be re-executed to produce the corresponding segmentation map (this bears

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similarity to the approach taken in [23], where a generative model is employed to model hand pose

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimation).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Aside from the ability to capture arbitrary modes with their corresponding probability conditioned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the input, our proposed Probabilistic U-Net allows to inspect its latent space. This is because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as opposed to e.g. GAN-based approaches, VAE-like models explicitly parametrize distributions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a characteristic that grants direct access to the corresponding likelihood landscape. Appendix A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discusses how the Probabilistic U-Net chooses to structure its latent spaces.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Compared to aforementioned concurrent work for image-to-image tasks [22], our model disentangles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the prior and the segmentation net. This can be of particular relevance in medical imaging, where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing 3D scans is common. In this case it is desirable to condition on the entire scan, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retaining the possibility to process the scan tile by tile in order to be able to process large volumes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with large models with a limited amount of GPU memory.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On a more general note, we would like to remark that current image-to-image translation tasks only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allow subjective (and expensive) performance evaluations, as it is typically intractable to assess the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entire solution space. For this reason surrogate metrics such as the inception score based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluation via a separately trained deep net are employed [36]. The task of multi-modal semantic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, which we consider here, allows for a direct and thus perhaps more meaningful manner

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of performance evaluation and could help guide the design of future generative architectures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All in all we see a large field where our proposed Probabilistic U-Net can replace the currently applied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deterministic U-Nets. Especially in the medical domain, with its often ambiguous images and highly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical decisions that depend on the correct interpretation of the image, our model's segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hypotheses and their likelihoods could 1) inform diagnosis/classification probabilities or 2) guide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steps to resolve ambiguities. Our method could prove useful beyond explicitly multi-modal tasks, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the inspectability of the Probabilistic U-Net's latent space could yield insights for many segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks that are currently treated as a uni-modal problem.
